samples.summary: New nonce ingestion in GitHubAuthGuard has no test at all
samples.evidence: The guard now reads `req.query.nonce` and applies real validation logic (must be a string, non-empty, <= MAX_NONCE_LENGTH=128) before forwarding it to `cliAuthStore.createState`. Grepping the backend for `GitHubAuthGuard`/`github-auth.guard` returns only auth.controller.ts, auth.module.ts and the guard itself — there is no `github-auth.guard.spec.ts` (only auth.controller, auth.service, jwt.strategy, github.strategy, cli-auth.store specs exist). So nothing covers: nonce forwarded on the happy path, an over-length nonce being dropped, an array-valued `?nonce=a&nonce=b` query (Express gives an array — `typeof !== 'string'` → undefined, silently disabling the binding check), or an empty nonce. This is the entry point of the whole anti-code-injection chain and it is entirely untested; the controller test only exercises the store→redirect half.

samples.summary: The `no nonce → no state param` branch of the redirect is not asserted
samples.evidence: `stateEcho` is a ternary with two branches. The new spec ('echoes the CLI nonce back as `state`', auth.controller.spec.ts:217) only covers the nonce-present branch. The pre-existing test at auth.controller.spec.ts:205 asserts `stringMatching(/^http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:9876\/callback\?code=.+/)`, which matches whether or not `&state=` is appended, so it cannot detect a regression (e.g. emitting `&state=undefined`) in the empty branch.

samples.summary: cli-auth.store.spec was not updated for the new `nonce` field
samples.evidence: `createState` gained a third parameter and `consumeState` now returns `nonce`, but cli-auth.store.spec.ts still calls `store.createState('browser', 9876)` and asserts `toEqual({ csrf, mode, port })`. Jest's `toEqual` ignores `undefined` properties, so that assertion passes regardless of whether the nonce is stored or returned. No test in this spec round-trips a nonce through createState/consumeState; the only coverage is indirect, via the controller test.

samples.summary: CLI side: nothing tests that the OAuth start URL carries the same nonce the callback server expects
samples.evidence: login-callback.test.ts calls `startCallbackServer('the-nonce')` directly with a literal. The `login` action — which mints `randomBytes(32)`, passes it to `startCallbackServer(nonce)` AND embeds it in `${server}/auth/github?...&nonce=...` — has no test. A regression where the two diverge (e.g. one is encoded/truncated differently) would leave every real login failing the state check while the shipped test stays green.

samples.summary: Wrong-state case only exercises the length-mismatch short circuit, not timingSafeEqual
samples.evidence: `nonceMatches` returns false via `a.length === b.length && timingSafeEqual(...)`. The test's wrong state is `guessed` (7 bytes) against `the-nonce` (9 bytes), so the comparison short-circuits on length and `timingSafeEqual` never runs. An equal-length-but-different state (the realistic guess against a fixed-width base64url nonce) is never exercised.

samples.summary: `command: commandPath(this)` plumbing into the orchestrators is untested
samples.evidence: files.ts, docs.ts, notes.ts and slides.ts now pass `command: commandPath(this)` into runFilesUpload/runFilesDownload/runDocsImport/runNotesImport/runSlidesImport. The orchestrator suites call those functions directly without a `command` arg (grep for `command` in packages/cli/test/files-download.test.ts returns nothing; notes-import/slides-import/docs-import only assert `error.code`), and output.test.ts's end-to-end attribution tests cover only docs.get, sheets.cells.get, docs.content and schema — none of the orchestrator commands. So a dropped or wrong `command` on e.g. `files upload` would not fail any test.

samples.summary: Fingerprint fixture not updated for the new `command` field in the envelope
samples.evidence: hunt-probe.mjs's doc comment now advertises `{"error":{"code":"ERROR","message":"fetch failed","command":"docs.get"}}`, but hunt-fingerprint.test.mjs:74 still fingerprints the old two-field envelope. Nothing checks whether the added `command` field changes `observedKey`/fingerprint bucketing (i.e. whether the same defect now fingerprints differently per command).

finding.summary: New nonce ingestion in GitHubAuthGuard has no test at all
finding.evidence: The guard now reads `req.query.nonce` and applies real validation logic (must be a string, non-empty, <= MAX_NONCE_LENGTH=128) before forwarding it to `cliAuthStore.createState`. Grepping the backend for `GitHubAuthGuard`/`github-auth.guard` returns only auth.controller.ts, auth.module.ts and the guard itself — there is no `github-auth.guard.spec.ts` (only auth.controller, auth.service, jwt.strategy, github.strategy, cli-auth.store specs exist). So nothing covers: nonce forwarded on the happy path, an over-length nonce being dropped, an array-valued `?nonce=a&nonce=b` query (Express gives an array — `typeof !== 'string'` → undefined, silently disabling the binding check), or an empty nonce. This is the entry point of the whole anti-code-injection chain and it is entirely untested; the controller test only exercises the store→redirect half.

verdict.reason: The guard's nonce ingestion is real and untested. github-auth.guard.ts:22-45 reads req.query.nonce and applies validation (string, non-empty, <= MAX_NONCE_LENGTH=128 at lines 6, 34-38) before passing it to cliAuthStore.createState. No test anywhere references the guard: a repo-wide grep for GitHubAuthGuard|github-auth matched only auth.controller.ts, auth.module.ts, the guard itself and .agent-review artifacts; no github-auth.guard.spec.ts exists while other guards do have specs (combined-auth.guard.spec.ts, workspace-scope.guard.spec.ts, yorkie-signature.guard.spec.ts). No indirect coverage either: none of the 17 e2e specs in packages/backend/test mention nonce or mode=cli, and no spec/test issues a request to /auth/github. The only nonce tests cover other halves of the chain — auth.controller.spec.ts:217-231 seeds the nonce by calling cliAuthStore.createState directly (bypassing the guard), and packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts:12,27 tests the CLI-side match. So the happy-path forwarding, the length cap, the empty-string case and the array-valued ?nonce=a&nonce=b case are all uncovered. Missing test for a changed behavior = major under the test-adequacy rubric.

mergedFrom.summary: Alias test is vacuous — it never reaches the command by alias

finding.summary: The "reached by alias" test never goes through an alias — it is tautological
finding.evidence: `it('reports the canonical name when the command was reached by alias')` builds `program.command('docs').alias('doc')` and then calls `outputError(new Error('boom'), docs.command('content'))` directly. No argv is ever parsed, so the command is not "reached by alias" in any sense; the test passes the canonical `Command` object itself. `commandPath` (src/output/formatter.ts:58-64) reads `c.name()`, which in commander always returns the canonical name and never the alias, so this assertion is true regardless of whether alias handling works — including if `.alias('doc')` were deleted entirely. The behavior it claims to guard (running `wafflebase doc content …` and getting `command:"docs.content"` in the envelope) would require `parseAsync(['node','wafflebase','doc','content'])` and inspecting the emitted envelope; no such test exists in this file.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the alias test "never goes through an alias": that it calls `outputError(new Error('boom'), docs.command('content'))` directly and that "no argv is ever parsed". The code is not as described. packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:205-218 registers `.command('docs').alias('doc').command('content')` with an `.action(function (this: Command) { outputError(new Error('boom'), this); })` and then executes `await program.parseAsync(['node','wafflebase','doc','content'])`, asserting on the envelope actually emitted to stderr via the `console.error` spy (`getEmittedBody()`, lines 147-158, which also asserts the spy was called exactly once). That is precisely the test the reviewer says does not exist in this file. The test is falsifiable: with `createProgram()` (packages/cli/src/commands/root.ts:42-63) setting no `exitOverride` or unknown-command handling, deleting `.alias('doc')` would prevent commander from resolving the `doc` subcommand, the action would never fire, and both `toHaveBeenCalledOnce()` and the `'docs.content'` assertion would fail. The reviewer appears to have conflated this with the separate nested-command test at lines 193-198, which does legitimately call `outputError` directly for a different case. `commandPath` at packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:58-64 is quoted correctly but is exercised here through a real alias parse, so the coverage is genuine, not vacuous.
